title: Unit-normalized lisse section pullback between weakly contractible component lifts
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Let $U,V$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] with w-contractible coordinate rings [sk-def-pe-wlocal], let $S$ be an extremally disconnected profinite space, and fix homeomorphisms $\pi_0(U)\cong S\cong\pi_0(V)$ of quotient component spaces [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Let $g:V\to U$ be a scheme morphism inducing $\operatorname{id}_S$. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the pulled-back coefficients $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and ordinary unbounded module derived categories and derived pullbacks [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use compatible small-site universes [def-weil-size-convention]. On profinite spaces over $S$ use finite jointly surjective coverings and coefficient $\Lambda_S$, the restriction of $\Lambda$. Write $\pi_T$ for the component morphism induced by $E\mapsto T\times_S E$ [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site].
The projection-preserving isomorphisms
$$V\times_S E\cong V\times_U(U\times_S E)$$
for profinite $E\to S$ induce a canonical monoidal comparison $g^*\pi_U^*\cong\pi_V^*$ on derived module categories, compatible with the coefficient units and with composition in $E$ and $g$. For every finite-rank lisse $\Lambda_U$-module $L$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], $g^*L$ is finite-rank lisse. The complexes $L[0]$ and $g^*L[0]$ have locally finite free module duals, are K-flat (tensoring with any acyclic complex gives an acyclic complex) [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and are dualizable for ordinary derived tensor: their evaluation and coevaluation satisfy both triangle identities.
For any dualizable $N$ on $S$ and any isomorphism $\pi_U^*N\cong L[0]$, the component equivalences on dualizable objects [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] identify the actual pullback map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_U[0],L[0])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_V[0],g^*L[0])$$
with the identity on $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_S[0],N)$. Here dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation with both triangle identities. Under the evaluation-on-$1$ identifications of these two Hom groups with $\Gamma(U,L)$ and $\Gamma(V,g^*L)$ [def-sfb-condensed-module-sections], this map is exactly the section pullback induced by the module adjunction unit and the coefficient isomorphism. In particular the actual map $\Gamma(U,L)\to\Gamma(V,g^*L)$ is bijective, naturally in $L$ and compatibly with composition in $g$. No discreteness, completeness or t-admissibility assumption on $\Lambda$ is made, and varying finite ranks, rank zero and empty schemes are included.

proof.text: Use the coherent geometric comparison theorem to choose d,m,c, the induced test and module comparisons, their monoidality, component equivalences and composition law.
Apply isLisseCoefficientModule_upperStar to L. Use finite-free duality on L and its pullback; the derived ExactPairing proves that L[0] is dualizable.

The monoidal unit equation for c inverse and its naturality at b prove ComponentLiftHomIdentity. Essential surjectivity of F_U on dualizable objects gives N and a:F_U N≅L[0]. The two bijections from Hom(1,N), obtained by full faithfulness of F_U and F_V and pre/postcomposition with the specified unit and object isomorphisms, identify the normalized derived pullback with the identity. Evaluation at one intertwines this normalized pullback with the specified section map. Cancel the source parametrization and use bijectivity of the target parametrization to obtain bijectivity of the actual section map. These are the private Lean lemmas normalized_naturality, parametrization_bijective and component_sections_bijective, proved without holes.

Assemble these assertions with evaluation bijectivity, section naturality and the identity and composition laws. The geometric composition law gives the first clause, and the normalization theorem gives the section-composition clause.
